subject: 3code
title: Anti-approval thesis implemented as product: no approval code exists anywhere in the tool path; the default-on kernel fence is the sole enforcement
evidence: docs/manual.md:1244-1258 (thesis: judge models = security-by-vibes, approvals = interruption-training); zero confirm/approve hits in engine.nim/turns.nim/actions.nim; tools dispatch straight into fence: streamexec.nim:591-652 (box-wrapped bash), sandbox.nim:499 (checkRawPath), sandbox.nim:164 (checkRawHost)
one_why: Corpus design-position datapoint: approval-first (codex), fence+floor (minicode), and now true fence-only - the only subject that removed the approval rung entirely rather than layering it, and says so with an honest calibration of what the fence does not stop.

subject: 3code
title: Default policy ends with allow * : filesystem fence ships on, network egress ships fully open; net fence opt-in only once a host rule appears
evidence: src/threecode/sandbox.nim:64-83 (defaultPolicyText: deny / + allow ./ + allow *), :164-167 (wallProxyNeeded: fencing off until first host rule)
one_why: Inversion of codex's separate egress-approval default: exfiltration - the primary coding-agent attack path - is unfenced out of the box; this is the specific hole capping 3code's safety at 7, and the cheapest fix in the corpus (default-deny hosts + an approval or prompt path).

subject: 3code
title: Kernel-backend failure degrades bash to unconfined - announced once on stderr with exactly what was lost, never refused
evidence: src/threecode.nim:168-169 (procboxExe cleared on probe fail), :477-486 (magenta warning: 'bash runs unconfined... read/write/patch tools stay confined'); src/threecode/streamexec.nim:555-556,653-660 (unconfined setsid fallback)
one_why: Honest pole of the fail-open family ledger: the degradation names what was LOST (inverse of claw-code's runtime-lie), and probe-hang is deliberately treated as confinement-kept (sandbox.nim:318-325) - but availability still outranks safety by default; confine-or-refuse (forge) remains the stricter posture.

subject: 3code
title: Byte-reproducible builds as a blocking gate: digest-pinned container, snapshot.ubuntu apt freeze, sha256-pinned Nim, double-clean-build compare, mtime-perturbed archive re-pack
evidence: .github/workflows/linux-amd64.yml:20-34 (image digest + snapshot archive), :56-64 (NIM_SHA256 pin), :86-97 (rebuild-identical + pack-twice-identical both fail the job)
one_why: Supply-chain ledger entry per the amazon-q rule - credited as supply-chain, not verification; the strongest self-documented reproducibility recipe in the T1 pool, including the toolchain-provenance BUILD_INFO capture for future same-toolchain comparison.

subject: 3code
title: Hidden guard rules lock the two activatable policy files read-only inside every sandboxed launch, appended last so no policy text can weaken them, and never rendered to the user
evidence: src/threecode/sandbox.nim:404-435 (guardRules appended after every parse), box.nim:16-25 (same guards re-applied in the box child; Landlock ro-under-writable-root caveat documented as accepted)
one_why: Self-protection of the confinement policy against the confined process AND against the policy file itself - with the rare move of documenting the one backend (Landlock rule-union) where the lock does not fully subtract, rather than overclaiming it.

subject: 3code
title: In-process tool gate reimplements the OS backend's path canonicalization and is drift-guarded by named traversal regressions
evidence: src/threecode/sandbox.nim:450-497 (resolveRawPath mirrors sandwall normalize, symlink-resolving deepest-existing-ancestor), :499-524 (checkRawPath); tests/core/test_sandbox_traversal.nim:1-12 (escape fixture: proj/sub/../../../etc/passwd)
one_why: Two enforcement paths (in-process read/write/patch gate vs kernel box) must decide identically or the weaker one is the real policy; the traversal suite exists precisely because lexical-prefix checks pass symlink/.. escapes - reuse-first note: same drift-parity concept as codebuff-b5, different axis (gate vs backend rather than duplicate algorithms).

subject: 3code
title: Zero-token doom-loop breaker: fingerprint window + streak ring with Jaccard near-duplicate clustering, escalation ladder of three injected messages, then turn abort
one_why: Nuance on the canonical loop-detection idiom: similarity-fingerprinted rather than exact-repeat, and the countermeasure is an escalating message ladder because (per the cited GLM-5 field report at turns.nim:57-58) a plain warning does not break an already-committed thinking loop.

subject: 3code
title: Policy reloaded by mtime before every restricted operation AND re-loaded by each sandbox child, so a mid-session policy edit can only tighten what the next launch enforces
evidence: src/threecode/sandbox.nim:426-435 (reloadIfChanged before every check), box.nim:11-14 (child loads --policy itself: a parent-vs-child race can only tighten)
one_why: Turns config-file staleness from a silent security gap into a monotonic-tightening property - the enforcement-side twin of the narrowing-monotone invariant (dvalincode); cheap to copy: mtime check + child-side load.
